<reason>A razor-close, high-skill debate decided by motion-anchored framing and unanswered pressure. A anchored everything to the motion as written: a conjunctive claim asserting parity as settled fact plus a policy command covering custody, donor conception, and adoption — and showed the universal declaration outruns evidence B ultimately concedes doesn't exist at population scale. A's triage/statute distinction neutralized B's central foster-child device while directly answering the dilemma ("place her — today; it concedes nothing"), and A landed the sharpest unresolved hit: B made stability decisive in the opening, then called separation possibly benign when it cut the other way, with no evidence offered that legal recognition closes the dissolution gap. B's scope was never extended beyond adoption triage to donor conception or custody, a gap A named twice. B's convergence-vs-scatter argument, confound critique, and exposure-measurement criterion were genuinely strong and partially recovered the administrative-data asymmetry charge, keeping this competitive, but B was clipped twice and left more weighty points standing. Both sides showed excellent epistemic discipline — no fake citations or brittle precision — and both answered pressure questions in proper format.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's A2 in Rebuttal 2: facing B's foster-child dilemma (couple or group home?), A conceded the placement head-on, then severed it from the motion — emergency triage compares a couple to an institution, while the statute declares a parent's sex irrelevant universally across custody, donor conception, and adoption law. This disarmed B's most powerful device without evasion, and B's closing counter ("screening room and statute should not answer differently") arrived too late to fully rebuild it. Runner-up: A's dissolution sequence ("evidence they hope will exist later"; "instability is decisive when useful, harmless when measured in the wrong families"), which exposed a genuine tension in B's case that B never squarely resolved.</best_rebuttal>
